seoTitle: How to Use QuickBooks With eBay Easily (2026)
metaDescription: Connect QuickBooks Online to eBay with the eBay Connector app: where the panel lives, the one-year limit on historical orders, and how long a new sale takes to show up.
intro: Running an eBay store on top of QuickBooks means the same sale exists in two places until you connect them: once as a listing and payout on eBay, once as income and fees in your books. QuickBooks doesn't build eBay syncing into the core product. It's handled through the eBay Connector, an app you add from the integrations panel inside your QuickBooks Online account. This guide covers where that panel lives, what the connection flow looks like, and the two limits Intuit's own documentation states but doesn't put front and center: a one-year cap on how far back historical orders can be pulled, and a sync delay of a few hours rather than instant.
prerequisites: Admin or company-owner access in QuickBooks Online, since installing an app requires that level of permission

steps.heading: Get your chart of accounts ready first
steps.body: Before connecting anything, make sure QuickBooks has somewhere sensible for eBay activity to land: an income account for sales, an expense account for eBay and PayPal fees, and a bank or clearing account matching whatever account eBay pays out to. Skipping this doesn't break the connection, but the first sync dumps transactions into "Uncategorized Income" and "Uncategorized Expense," which you then clean up by hand. A few minutes naming accounts before you connect saves a longer cleanup session after.

steps.heading: Open Integrations from the QuickBooks toolbar
steps.body: Once you're in QuickBooks Online, look at the icon row in the top right of the screen, next to help and settings. This opens the Integrations panel (some regions still label it My integrations), the hub for every third-party connection attached to your account, not only eBay. From here, select Find integrations and search for "eBay Connector by Intuit," which is the app's official name in Intuit's own app store.

image.caption: The integrations panel, opened from the icon row at the top of QuickBooks Online — the starting point for adding the eBay Connector.

steps.heading: Install the connector and authorize eBay
steps.body: Select Get app now, then follow the setup flow into a "Connect your accounts" screen showing the QuickBooks and eBay logos side by side. Clicking Continue takes you into eBay's own login flow to grant permission, so you're authorizing access rather than typing your eBay password into a QuickBooks form. Read what the connector actually does before continuing: Intuit's documentation lists importing order net amount, fees, taxes, discounts, products and services, and customers.

image.caption: The eBay Connector's account-linking screen, laying out the steps to sign in, review sync settings, and bring in eBay data.

steps.heading: Set your sync settings, including how far back to import
steps.body: After authorizing, you choose sync settings before anything imports blind: which eBay account or store to sync if you run more than one, and how far back to pull historical orders. Intuit caps this at up to one year of historical orders, a limit the app doesn't always surface clearly during setup, so don't expect a full multi-year backlog even if you request it.

steps.heading: Give new orders a few hours, then categorize what lands
steps.body: New eBay orders, fees, and payouts don't appear the instant a sale happens. Intuit's support documentation says imported orders typically show up in the App transactions page's Imported tab within about four hours. Once they land, the first batch almost always needs manual categorization until you've matched transaction types to the accounts you set up in step one; QuickBooks then starts suggesting the same category for similar future transactions.

steps.heading: Reconcile weekly and know how to disconnect
steps.body: Check the connection weekly rather than assuming it runs flawlessly forever. Connector apps occasionally need re-authorization if eBay changes its permissions, and catching that quickly keeps your books from silently falling behind. If you ever need to remove it, go back to Integrations, select Manage integrations, and disconnect from the eBay Connector's app card.

tables.title: Where eBay Connector data typically lands
rows: An income account dedicated to eBay sales
An expense account for marketplace fees
A bank or clearing account matching eBay's payout destination
tables.note: Set these up before connecting; the app applies whatever mapping you choose during sync setup rather than creating one for you.

faq.question: Does QuickBooks connect to eBay natively, without any add-on?
faq.answer: No. The connection is made through the eBay Connector by Intuit, added from the Integrations panel inside QuickBooks Online, not a built-in feature.

faq.question: Where do I find the integrations panel in QuickBooks Online?
faq.answer: The icon row in the top right of the QuickBooks Online toolbar, next to settings and help. Opening it shows Integrations (or My integrations, depending on region) and every app connected to your account.

faq.question: Does QuickBooks ever see my eBay password?
faq.answer: No. Authorization happens through eBay's own sign-in flow when you connect the eBay Connector, so QuickBooks receives permission to sync data, not your login credentials.

faq.question: How far back will my past eBay sales import?
faq.answer: Up to one year of historical orders, per Intuit's own documentation. You choose the exact start date during setup, but the app won't reach further back than that regardless of what you select.

faq.question: Why don't new sales show up in QuickBooks right away?
faq.answer: There's a sync delay. Intuit's support documentation states that new orders usually appear in the Imported tab within about four hours, not instantly.

faq.question: Why are my first synced transactions showing as uncategorized?
faq.answer: New connections often land in generic accounts until you manually categorize the first batch and QuickBooks learns to apply the same category to similar future transactions.
